top_choice_rationale: P001 (B001: Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) is the only proposal on the slate and I rank it above no award. The achievement is a measurement advance: estimating demand and competition in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices. It recovers substitution patterns, markups and welfare counterfactuals that reduced-form work could not, it has been used in merger review and regulation, and it has spread to trade, health and environmental economics. About three decades of re-implementation on different data, algorithms and instruments have exposed its numerical and identification weaknesses, and those are now documented. That is the nearest thing this literature has to a many-analyst replication, and it is the stress-testing I weight most. The credit is also compact, since the core 1995 paper has these three authors. The reservations are real. It is a toolkit, Bresnahan is omitted, and I have not verified how often the known sensitivities reverse a merger or welfare conclusion. The citation should be worded so that it does not overstate precision. These reservations do not outweigh the case for awarding the prize this year.
